details:
EARTHBEARS

Earth Analogs for the Moon and Mars An interactive comparison of places on Earth with their counterparts on the lunar South Pole and on Mars. It shows where each analog matches and, just as clearly, where it does not.

Built for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge.

Challenge: Identify Earth Locations that Analog the Permanent Moon Base Locations and Mars Team: EARTHBEARS Members: Zeyna ALKHATIB, Yiğit SEZER Local event: Eskişehir local event Project page:

This is a student project. It is not a NASA product and is not endorsed by NASA. What it does The project opens on a cover page with two parts. Part 1: Moon – Lunar South Pole in 3D A 3D model of the lunar south-pole geologic map next to two polar sites on Earth: Haughton crater (Devon Island, Canada) and McMurdo Sound (Antarctica). Rotate, zoom and change the light direction. Click a lunar rock unit in the legend to see the Earth rock it resembles, with a 1–5 similarity rating. A table for each site rates 17 aspects as similar, different, or a minor or tolerable difference. A thought experiment: what would have to change for each site to look like the Moon? Part 2: Mars – 12 Mars–Earth pairs Twelve Martian regions paired with Earth sites, for example Jezero Crater and Lake Salda (Türkiye), or Valles Marineris and the Grand Canyon. A Mars map and an Earth map that move together when you pick a pair. Magnified close-ups side by side. Cards for each pair: coordinates, landform, how it formed, and temperature. How to run it No installation and no build step.

Download or clone this repository. Open index.html in a modern browser (Chrome, Edge or Firefox). Choose Moon or Mars on the cover. Use the bar at the top to switch between them or return to the cover.

The 3D library and the page styles are embedded in the files, so the project works without an internet connection. Only the web font on the Mars page needs a connection; without one, the browser uses a system font. Publish with GitHub Pages Push the files to a public repository, keeping index.html in the repository root. In the repository, go to Settings → Pages. Under Build and deployment, choose Deploy from a branch, select the main branch and the / (root) folder, then save. After a minute or two the site is available at https://.github.io//. Put that link at the top of this file. Other material:

Earth site imagery in the Moon page comes from Google Earth (© Google). The 3D relief in the Moon page is an estimate made for illustration. It is not measured elevation data. Limits Similarity ratings are our own judgment. They are not published equivalences. Earth cannot reproduce lunar or Martian gravity, vacuum, radiation or permanent shadow. The comparison covers landform, geology, temperature, ice and light only.
